evidence.text: Choose a positive tail value, then a farther point with a smaller value. Maximizing between the nonpositive interior endpoint and the farther tail point produces a positive stationary point. In a field theory, separately verify stationarity in all transverse directions.

evidence.text: Apply Euler's theorem to ln𝒱, differentiate once, and use the relation between real and complex derivatives to derive inverse-metric contractions. This avoids constructing the complete inverse metric for an arbitrary number of Kähler moduli.

evidence.text: Construct both cone approximations, dualize them, impose stabilization constraints, and integrate the induced metric. Refine the outer Kähler domain when its length diverges, because a divergent overestimate cannot decide whether the physical domain has finite range.

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: A stabilized type-IIB Kähler modulus must remain locally stable when positive supersymmetry-breaking energy is added. The baseline model combines a logarithmic Kähler potential, a flux constant, a single condensate exponential, and an anti-D3 energy proportional to the inverse square of the volume modulus.

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: Two confining gauge sectors coupled to one Kähler modulus can provide competing exponentials that separate the stabilized modulus mass from the vacuum energy. The same competition produces axion interference and motivates checking both the assumed superpotential and the resulting field-distance scales.

sources.title: Racing through the swampland: de Sitter uplift vs weak gravity

evidence.text: What is the actual holomorphic superpotential when two confining gauge sectors share a perturbatively massless dynamical coupling modulus? Determining its branch structure could decide whether the long-period interference assumed in racetrack stabilization survives.

sources.title: Emergent strings, duality and weak coupling limits for two-form fields

evidence.text: Decompose D3 tangent and normal representations, perform the twist, retain neutral supercharges, and count zero modes. For a square-zero genus-one curve in K3, this yields a two-dimensional N=(4,4) spectrum without a duality twist.

sources.title: Some comments on string dynamics

evidence.text: Translate BPS-protected type-IIA W masses through circle T-duality. Their type-IIB mass proportional to circle circumference identifies winding strings, modeled by a self-dual three-brane wrapped on a shrinking K3 two-sphere.

sources.title: Emergent strings, duality and weak coupling limits for two-form fields

evidence.text: Determine wrapped-brane modes, separate transverse positions, identify the internal moduli space, and take the shrinking-cycle limit. In this application the reported target is B3; a further duality argument identifies the emergent Type IIB string.

sources.title: Emergent strings, duality and weak coupling limits for two-form fields

evidence.text: Reduce the bulk kinetic term and brane Chern–Simons term in compatible bases, compute internal Hodge products, and impose the tensor duality constraint. The simplified output requires (1,1) forms and the unfluxed wrapped-brane setup.

sources.title: Some comments on string dynamics

evidence.text: Use linear sigma models, hyperkähler quotient coordinates A²+BC=0 and superconformal R-current constraints to study branch separation. The conifold analogue uses W=P(XY+ZT−ε), with an additional P branch at ε=0.

sources.title: Some comments on string dynamics

evidence.text: For large-circle reduction, organize the radius potential using massless-particle Feynman diagrams: the leading Casimir term scales as −(nB−nF)/r³, and higher inverse powers require higher-dimensional terms in the low-energy effective action.

destination.title: Stochastic survival and calculational control
destination.question: When do quantum inflaton fluctuations sustain inflation after accounting for classical motion, escape from the inflating region and control of the fluctuation calculation?
destination.summary: Distinguishes a local kick-versus-drift diagnostic from sustained production of inflating regions. Finite hilltops, rare recycling and transient turnaround proposals require separate survival analyses.

systems: Hilltops, inflection regions and specified chaotic potentials
regimes: Source-specific slow-roll, turnaround and beyond-slow-roll regimes
assumptions: The usual free-field kick is conditional on its fluctuation regime
A finite quantum-dominated interval need not imply global termination
conventions: Keep local, worldline and volume-based meanings of persistence distinct
excludes: Automatic equivalence with defect or false-vacuum persistence

sources.title: Eternal Hilltop Inflation

evidence.text: The authors describe the field using a Langevin equation and approximate its escape from a finite interval by a random walk. They combine an estimated inflating fraction ΓI∝exp(−t/⟨t⟩) with volume growth exp(3Ht), testing whether the resulting inflating-volume exponent is positive.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Evaluate the assumed Gaussian jump exponent and add the logarithm of the available patch multiplicity. Requiring an order-one expected count gives a duration scale proportional to C²(M_P/H_end)².

evidence.text: Shift Eq. (7) to the turnaround using Ce⁻³ᴴᵗ* = cHmP, solve the absolute-value inequality without time expansion, and compare the two crossings. The result is an analytical audit within the source's approximation, not a stochastic inflation calculation.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation, Entropy Bounds and the Swampland

evidence.text: Compare deterministic drift and stochastic displacement over one Hubble interval, then express the result through potential derivatives using specified background approximations.

sources.title: Dimensional reduction and (Anti) de Sitter bounds

evidence.text: Convert de Sitter variance growth into diffusion, solve for the probability distribution, integrate over inflating field values, and compare the resulting decay rate against physical-volume expansion.

sources.title: Eternal Hilltop Inflation

evidence.text: Slow-roll formulas for ε,η, the e-fold count N and the horizon-exit spectrum P=H²/(8π²MP²ε) relate the quantum-dominated width to potential parameters. The observed amplitude and spectral tilt are then used to assess the width-to-kick condition.

sources.title: Topological Eternal Hilltop Inflation and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: What maintains a hilltop configuration after inflation starts? The topological mechanism invokes a persistent defect retaining the potential maximum at its center, while the stochastic mechanism invokes fluctuating field trajectories.

evidence.text: A coarse-grained scalar in quasi-de Sitter space undergoes classical potential-driven drift and random horizon-crossing fluctuations. The competition determines how long regions remain inflationary.

evidence.text: How do a canonical inflaton's potential, classical motion, and expansion rate determine whether quantum fluctuations can dominate? The background is flat FLRW, with potential energy providing nearly de Sitter expansion.

evidence.text: Can competition between slow-roll horizon growth and matter-induced contraction diagnose whether inflation ends?

evidence.text: Can self-reproduction occur in the simple massive or quartic regimes of an assisted chaotic potential? The two contributions share a common field amplitude and total Hubble friction, but the conjectured cutoff remains tied to the quartic coupling.

evidence.text: Can a canonical scalar near a positive cosine maximum support stochastic eternal inflation and subsequently enter a sufficiently long, observationally acceptable rolling phase?

evidence.text: Can self-reproducing chaotic inflation approach a stationary statistical description, despite continuing expansion and nonstationary comoving fields? The paper distinguishes recurring local domain properties from global stationarity of probability distributions.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: How do a single inflaton's potential slope and quantum fluctuations compare during approximately de Sitter expansion? The analysis uses potential-dominated slow roll and a canonically normalized scalar, as implicit in the displayed evolution equations.

evidence.text: Do quantum-gravity principles and selected phenomenological models obstruct slow-roll or false-vacuum eternal inflation, and do these obstructions suggest a general prohibition?

sources.title: Stochastic eternal inflation is in the swampland

evidence.text: Do explicit fluctuation-control requirements similarly restrict inflation when extra degrees of freedom affect scalar dynamics, as in warm inflation, or when the inflating source is not a fundamental scalar? The paper identifies these questions without answering them.

sources.title: Stochastic eternal inflation is in the swampland

evidence.text: Can stochastic quantum kicks prolong single-field inflation in a potential whose small slope is accompanied by the negative curvature demanded by the refined de Sitter conjecture? The question includes whether the fluctuation calculation remains controlled.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and the Refined Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Can eternal inflation near a single-field potential maximum coexist with the refined de Sitter conjecture? The comparison concerns a tachyonic hilltop branch that avoids the original positive-gradient requirement.

sources.title: Steep Eternal Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: When does a light inflaton's typical quantum displacement over a Hubble time exceed its classical displacement? The paper uses this comparison to identify diffusion zones and motivate continued inflation in some spatial regions.

sources.title: Stochastic eternal inflation is in the swampland

evidence.text: The setting asks when quantum fluctuations can compete with classical inflaton motion while spacetime remains semiclassical. Higher-derivative interactions are represented through a sound speed, but the central curvature argument uses the unit-sound-speed limit.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation in Swampy Landscapes

evidence.text: Can an eternally inflating multiverse exist when positive-energy minima are rare, or when all minima are nonpositive and hilltops cannot support stochastic eternal inflation?

sources.title: Steep Eternal Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: The setting concerns quantum versus classical inflaton evolution in Einstein gravity. A conventional slow-roll comparison and a separate acceleration-retaining turnaround calculation share potential domination, but their scalar equations of motion use different approximations.

sources.title: Eternal inflation in light of Wheeler-DeWitt equation

evidence.text: Can higher-excitation solutions of the semiclassical Wheeler–DeWitt equation enlarge inflaton-displacement uncertainty and relax eternal-inflation conditions, and do nonlinear interactions or entropy favor the lowest excitation?

sources.title: Quantum cosmology, eternal inflation, and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: How do tunneling nucleation, the scalar quantum state, and stochastic eternal inflation change beyond slow roll near a potential maximum? Do their transition thresholds coincide when m/H is of order one?

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can self-reproducing inflation coexist with a finite effective-theory field range and a lower bound on the gradient of a positive scalar potential? The paper studies this compatibility conditionally, with explicit calculations for one slowly rolling inflaton.

sources.title: Power spectrum of density perturbations in chain inflation

evidence.text: The illustration asks how stochastic inflaton evolution can be evaluated inside the past light cone of an observer at time \(10H^{-1}\). Physical position and time are displayed in Hubble units, with the evaluation point at the top.

sources.title: Rejuvenating the hope of a swampland consistent inflated multiverse with tachyonic inflation in the high-energy RS-II braneworld

evidence.text: The setting replaces an ordinary scalar inflaton by a square-root tachyon field. Its kinetic normalization matters when translating potential derivatives, field excursions and quantum fluctuation amplitudes into swampland and eternal-inflation criteria.

evidence.text: The local potential family tests whether inflation can persist near a maximum or inflection point while quantum kicks compete with outward classical drift. The retained quadratic term matters for satisfying a finite tachyonic-curvature requirement.
